author: Carol and Kent (nomad_kiwis)
citation: the first night we didn't find it and ended up sleeping on a beach on the way and finding the gathering the next day. We have now been camping there since the 1st of November, on a beach north of La Paz
location: Beach north of La Paz, Baja California, Mexico
provenance: Travel journal entry by New Zealand travelers Carol and Kent on WorldNomads, November 2008, recounting sleeping on a beach while searching for a Rainbow gathering and subsequently camping on the sand.

author: Claudia Tavani
citation: I was finally granted permission to sleep under some palm trees, at the beach. We pitched the tent using only a flashlight as illumination... and despite being really uncomfortable, I fell asleep soon afterwards.
location: Isla Porvenir, San Blas Islands (Guna Yala), Panama
provenance: First-person account by Claudia Tavani published on Bunch of Backpackers, June 2014, recounting an emergency overnight in a tent on the beach of Isla Porvenir after being dropped off from a sailing boat.

author: Walker R. (Danny Gottlieb)
citation: we put up our tent and the family began to pack up. We realized we might have an entire beach — an entire bay, from the looks of it — to ourselves. ... even when the breeze died, leaving the desert heat to bake us in our tent all night... we all still consider this night one of the greatest of our lives
location: White sand beach near Bahía Concepción, Baja California Sur, Mexico
provenance: Personal road trip account by Walker R. published on Lost Travel, March 2019, describing camping in a tent on a deserted beach near Bahía Concepción after getting lost with a paper map.
